key_insight: Replace the static one-to-one vision→LLM connector with a dynamic many-to-many cross-layer injection so the language model can access hierarchical visual features (local to global) for richer, more accurate multimodal reasoning.
problem_solved: Eliminates the visual feature bottleneck caused by routing only the vision encoder's final output into the LLM, which prevents alignment of multi-scale visual information and weakens grounding of local details within global semantics.
method: Introduce dynamic cross-layer injection modules that connect multiple vision-encoder layers to multiple LLM layers, enabling many-to-many information flow.
Use learned routing/gating or attention to select and fuse relevant hierarchical visual features per language layer, preserving multi-scale context.
Integrate lightweight adapters and alignment objectives so the mechanism is plug-and-play with existing VLMs while keeping compute and finetuning costs manageable.
impact: Enables stronger visual grounding and multi-scale reasoning in VLMs, improving accuracy on compositional and detail-sensitive tasks and making fusion architectures more flexible and extensible for practitioners.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: (a) traditional one-to-one bottleneck vs (b) proposed many-to-many cross-layer injections.

paper_title: From One-to-One to Many-to-Many: Dynamic Cross-Layer Injection for Deep Vision-Language Fusion
paper_authors: Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Peng Di
